connectionType: Authenticated event identity and contraction of order-preserving omission classes
strength: strong under an explicit one-to-one ordered-event model

commonStructure.UP-605: A process sample, metrology result, or twin residual must be joined to the exact wafer/chamber/tool event that generated it before source-to-target error can be transported.
commonStructure.UP-315: An exported frame must be joined to the exact camera trigger that generated it before one omission history can be distinguished from another.
commonStructure.shared: Both are partial matchings between a complete ordered reference roster E=(e1,...,eN) and an order-preserving observed subsequence Y=(y1,...,yM). Without join keys there are C(N,N-M) admissible histories; authenticated anchors partition the class, and a verified per-event identity makes the matching unique.

variableMapping.UP-605: missing, duplicated, or delayed production event
signed batch manifest and calibration clock
variableMapping.UP-315: counter-bound Merkle chunk and trigger clock

variableMapping.role: set of histories the evidence still permits

holdsWhen: The reference event roster is complete and its identity semantics are stable.
Each observation is generated by at most one reference event and surviving observations preserve reference order.
Counters, timestamps, or manifests are captured independently of the inferred image/process features and survive export unchanged.
Clock uncertainty is smaller than the separation needed to distinguish adjacent reference events, or an exact counter supplies the join.
breaksWhen: One observation integrates several events, several sensors contribute asynchronously, or events legitimately reorder.
The reference roster itself drops triggers or changes identity domains across reset, tool restart, recipe revision, or clock epoch.
A label is assigned after export by ordinal pairing; it then reproduces the assumption being tested rather than adding evidence.
A chunk signature authenticates bytes but no per-event counter identifies positions inside the chunk.
superficialSimilarityRisk: Both fields use words such as traceability and synchronization, but the connection is valid only after a one-to-one ordered matching is written down. A digital-twin feature vector averaged over a process window is not mathematically equivalent to a single camera exposure without a generative window model.

minimumValidationTest.design: Create an untouched event stream with a complete reference roster and inject one omission, duplicate, reorder, and clock reset at camera/measurement capture, export, and archive packaging. Freeze parsers and identity domains before opening the injected cases.
minimumValidationTest.success: Every injected fault is localized to its exact event identity with zero false localization, all clean controls remain clean, and an independent implementation reconstructs the same matching and Merkle proofs.
minimumValidationTest.failure: Any ordinal-only join, counter reset without a new domain identifier, ambiguous adjacent timestamp, false localization, or parser disagreement preserves the partial-matching class and blocks transport claims.

simultaneousImpact: A validated identity plane would not solve either scientific model by itself, but it would remove the shared provenance confounder. UP-605 could then test physical domain shift rather than record misalignment, while UP-315 could state which finite history was actually measured.
verifiedEvidence: RC48 independently reproduces the exact X16 count-only class and all anchor contractions in Node and Python.
The X16 public manifests, selected DAQ central directory, and 2025 compilation metadata expose no field passing the direct identity gate.
The EoSens camera supports an optional image counter, while RC45 shows that the tested public AVI bytes do not preserve it.
validationStatus: Mathematical contraction verified; public X16 identity channel absent from audited artifacts; prospective identity-plane experiment proposed
